one_liner: Intel's archived GPU-only C++ canvas (OpenGL/GLES); author's clip-heavy demo ran about 5-8x Skia GL's frame rate in 2016.
what_it_does: FastUIDraw is a canvas-style 2D API (fastuidraw::Painter) that always renders through a GPU via its GL 3.3 or GLES 3.0 backend. It covers stroking (including dashes and anti-aliasing), path filling with standard or custom fill rules, text from FreeType fonts, image and gradient brushes, Porter-Duff and advanced blend modes, a 3x3 (perspective) transform, save/restore, transparency layers, and clip-in/clip-out by rectangle, rounded rectangle or path. You also can plug in your own GLSL item, brush and blend shaders. It is its own API, not a Skia, Cairo or Qt backend, so callers port draw code to Painter calls and pre-build geometry objects such as StrokedPath, FilledPath and GlyphSequence.
how_it_is_fast: Everything is drawn by one uber-shader. Per-item state (transform, clip equations, brush, shader IDs) is packed into a data store, a texture buffer object by default, and each vertex reads a header from it. Canvas state changes therefore do not become GL state changes, and the README says only a blend-mode change forces a new pipeline state, so a frame needs only a handful of draw calls. Rectangle clip-in uses hardware clip planes (gl_ClipDistance by default). Clip-out and path clips use the depth buffer as an occluder (depth test GL_GEQUAL, z incremented per item), so changing the clip costs little more than drawing one occluding shape. Path tessellation, stroking geometry and glyph data are built once and reused, and images and glyphs live in GPU atlases so they cause no draw breaks.
when_to_use: UI or canvas scenes on desktop-class GPUs that change clip and transform state very often (many nested, clipped, rotating widgets per frame), which is the painter-cells workload behind the published numbers.
Linux or Windows (MinGW) apps that already own a GL 3.3 or GLES 3.0 context and want a 2D layer that issues very few draw calls.
Intel GPUs from Ivy Bridge on with recent Mesa or Intel Windows drivers, which the README says have every extension needed for all blend modes at full speed.
Studying or forking a GPU canvas design: uber-shader with packed data store, depth-buffer clipping, and custom shader chaining, all MPL-2.0.
when_not_to_use: Anything needing support or security fixes: Intel archived the repo on 2023-01-07 and accepts no patches. The last code commit is 2019-12-20, and questions about maintenance and Chromium integration (#61, #50) were never answered.
Machines without a real GPU driver: issue #19 measured 1.9 fps with Mesa's SWR software rasterizer against 32.7 fps for Cairo on an i3-4160 at 1280x1280.

Many short-lived or freshly built paths per frame. Issue #49 reported about 7x the CPU load of nanovg (around 29% CPU) on a line-drawing test at gcc 7.4 -O3, and it was closed without a recorded fix. The fast path assumes geometry is tessellated once and reused.
macOS (system GL headers unusable and the GL there is deprecated), WebGPU, Vulkan or Metal targets: there are only GL and GLES backends.
When you need Skia-level text shaping, color management, PDF or SVG output, or a CPU fallback: none of these is provided.

integration.form: shared lib (libFastUIDraw plus libFastUIDrawGL or libFastUIDrawGLES, release and debug variants, pkg-config files and a fastuidraw-config script)
integration.dependencies: FreeType; Khronos GL/GLES headers (glcorearb.h, khrplatform.h) supplied by the user; flex and perl at build time; SDL2 and SDL2_image for demos only; doxygen for docs
integration.min_toolchain: C++11 (-std=c++11), GNU Make, g++ (clang said to work); release libraries build at -O3 -fstrict-aliasing
integration.platforms: Linux and MinGW32/64 under MSYS2 per README; macOS only with copied Khronos headers ('Yes, this is a hack'); needs GL 3.3 or GLES 3.0, and blend modes beyond Porter-Duff need framebuffer fetch or fragment-shader interlock or ordering
integration.thread_safety: Not documented beyond notes: a Painter is a heavy, reference-counted object bound to a GL context, and shaders registered from a thread are not usable in that thread until the next begin(). Treat one Painter as single-threaded.

gotchas: Debug and release libraries must not be mixed; the README tells you to take matching flags from pkg-config or fastuidraw-config.

Benchmark mode (num_frames) times the gap between draw_frame calls, which includes buffer swap. Vsync is only disabled if you pass swap_interval 0 or set vblank_mode=0 on Mesa. The ports branch's bench.sh echoes vblank_mode=0 but actually runs with a misspelled 'vlank_mode=0'.
Images not on the atlas become bound textures when bindless texturing is missing, which breaks batching. The demo itself warns 'large performance impact expected'.
The first frames compile the uber-shader in the GL driver. Skip them (num_skip_frames) before timing anything.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick it over Pathfinder 3 or vger only if you need a full canvas feature set (clip-out by path, advanced blend modes, custom shaders) on GL and can live with an archived C++ codebase. For CPU rendering or maintained projects, Blend2D, Skia or ThorVG are the safer choices, and Rive Renderer and Vello are the maintained GPU-side options.
verified_claims_summary: The only numbers are first-party and known only from search snippets of Kevin Rogovin's XDC 2016 slides. In the painter-cells demo, frame rate normalized to Cairo's CPU image surface was FastUIDraw 9.33 vs Skia GL 1.91 at 25x12 cells and 11.11 vs 1.36 at 50x25 cells, on an unnamed Intel-GPU laptop, which is about 4.9x and 8.2x over Skia GL (derived from snippet data). Contrary to the record's caveat, the Qt, Cairo (xlib, image, GL) and Skia GL ports and the run scripts are public on the repo's with_ports_of_painter-cells branch (last updated 2018-12-20). The scripts ran 1920x1080 or 1920x1200 fullscreen, swap_interval 0, 25x12 cells, a 4000x2000 table, table and cells rotating and clipped, and images from /usr/share/games/blobwars/gfx. The Skia port's Makefile gives gn args (is_official_build=true, clang) and a tested Skia commit, 01979132133e. Two limits remain: the hardware is unnamed, and the branch's 2018-era Skia API (GrContext::MakeGL) is newer than the 2016 runs. The ports are also not fully equivalent. The Skia port calls SkCanvas::drawText on UTF-8 strings every frame, while FastUIDraw draws pre-formatted GlyphSequences. The Cairo port pre-lays out cairo_glyph_t arrays, and the Qt port was given QGlyphRun 'to make the comparison more fair'. That makes the Skia GL ratio somewhat favorable to FastUIDraw.
status_note: Abandoned: archived by Intel on 2023-01-07 with a discontinuation notice (last code change 2019-12-20). It is MPL-2.0 and copyable, but it is a large GL-specific codebase you would have to own outright.
